==English==

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:also|tree=1}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂el-|id=all}}{{word|en|ine|swé}}
From {{inh|en|enm|also}}, {{m|enm|alswo}}, {{m|enm|alswa}} (also {{m|enm|als|als(e)}}, {{m|enm|as}}, whence English {{m|en|as}}), from {{inh|en|ang|eallswā||just like, also}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*allswā}}, equivalent to {{com|en|all|so}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|alsa}}, {{m|sco|alswa||also, even so, in the same way, as, as well}}, {{cog|stq|also||accordingly, therefore, thus}}, {{cog|fy|alsa||so, just so, even so, thus}}, {{cog|osx|alsō||similarly, as if, just as, when}}, {{cog|nl|alzo||so, thus}}, {{cog|de|also||so, thus}}, {{cog|da|altså||so}}, {{cog|nb|altså||so, therefore, accordingly, thus}}, {{cog|nn|altso||so, accordingly, therefore, thus}}, {{cog|sv|alltså||so, therefore, accordingly, thus, then}}. {{doublet|en|as}}. More at {{m|en|all}}, {{m|en|so}}.

===Adverb===
{{en-adv|-}}

# {{lb|en|conjunctive|focus}} [[in addition|In addition]]; [[besides]]; [[as well]]; [[further]]; [[too]]. {{defdate|from 14<sup>th</sup> c.}}
#: {{ux|en|Everyone had eggs for breakfast, but Alice '''also''' had toast. '''Also''', she finished hers in under half an hour.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Also''' common are languages, like Latin, with a [[three-way]] distinction (''proximal, medial and distal'').}}
#: {{ux|en|When you withdraw yor forces, we shall '''also''' withdraw ours.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=1905|author=Bertrand Russell|journal=On Denoting
|passage=The subject of denoting is of very great importance, not only in logic and mathematics, but '''also''' in the theory of knowledge.}}
#* {{RQ:Belloc Lowndes Lodger|I|0016
|passage=Thus the red damask curtains which now shut out the fog-laden, drizzling atmosphere of the Marylebone Road, had cost a mere song, and yet they might have been warranted to last another thirty years. A great bargain '''also''' had been the excellent Axminster carpet which covered the floor;{{nb...}}.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2013|month=May-June|author=[http://www.americanscientist.org/authors/detail/katrina-g-claw Katrina G. Claw]
|title=[http://www.americanscientist.org/issues/feature/2013/3/rapid-evolution-in-eggs-and-sperm Rapid Evolution in Eggs and Sperm]
|volume=101|issue=3|magazine=w:American Scientist
|passage=Many genes with reproductive roles '''also''' have antibacterial and immune functions, which indicate that the threat of microbial attack on the sperm or egg may be a major influence on rapid evolution during reproduction.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} To the same [[degree]] or [[extent]]; [[so]], [[as]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=c. 1709|author=w:John Strype|title=Annals of the Reformation and Establishment of Religion
|passage={{...}} thereupon the queen's majesty {{...}} did send a solemn ambassade of her privy-counsellors, whereof one was an ancient earl of the realm, the other '''also''' an ancient baron of the same, and others of the council of her state {{...}}}}

====Usage notes====
The adverb '''also''' can go in various places within a sentence, with minimal change of meaning.
*{{ux|en|The golf courses are excellent. '''Also''', the tennis courts are fantastic.}}
*{{ux|en|The golf courses are excellent and the tennis courts are fantastic '''also'''.}}
*{{ux|en|Not only are the golf courses excellent but '''also''' the tennis courts are fantastic.}}
*{{ux|en|There are not just excellent golf courses here. There are '''also''' fantastic tennis courts.}}

In Norwegian non-native English, may be used in the beginning of sentence, because of confusing with the {{m+|nb|altså}} and {{m+|nn|altso}}.

====Synonyms====
* {{l|en|too}}
* {{l|en|eke}}
* {{l|en|as well}}
* {{l|en|so}}
